clue.text: Physicist had been a member before

parts.note: MP, a Member of Parliament, is the usual crossword member
ere is the poetic word for before

explanation.surface: A scientist who once sat in parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: André-Marie Ampère was the French physicist who gave his name to the unit of electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: Ampère was a French scientist working on electromagnetism, so he is an example of a physicist.

clue.text: Domestic had a mind to cook

indicators.note: to cook something is to doctor or rework it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A household servant fancies doing the cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic is a household servant, and a maid in service is one such female servant.

indicators.note: turned means the murderer's name is read backwards

parts.note: Cain, who killed Abel, is the Bible's first murderer

explanation.surface: A killer who dissolved victims in acid gives himself up.
explanation.definitionFit: Niacin is nicotinic acid, one of the B vitamins, so it is a kind of acid.

indicators.note: in places the numeral within the fruit's name

parts.note: ananas is another name for the pineapple
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A dishonest person hid something inside a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept' is only a link here. Ananias in Acts was struck dead for lying about money he had kept back.
explanation.definitionFit: Ananias is the biblical man punished for lying, and his name became a byword for a liar.

clue.text: Pretender takes up work without charges

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the whole construction is read from bottom to top
without in its old sense of outside, so the work goes round the charges

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
dues are fees or charges paid

explanation.surface: An impostor takes on a job that pays no fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense of outside, so the work wraps the charges; 'up', in a down clue, turns the whole assembly round.
explanation.definitionFit: A pseudo is a sham or someone putting on airs, which is what a pretender is.

indicators.note: improvement suggests the letters are worked into a better arrangement

explanation.surface: A meeting where everyone can notice progress.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'see' hints at the spiritualist's sitting, the medium hoping to see the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A séance is a sitting at which a medium tries to contact the dead, a kind of session.

clue.text: Time a pint's poured out — can't wait

indicators.note: pouring the drink out spills the letters into a new order

parts.note: the 's is short for is and gives no letter

explanation.surface: A drinker eager for a pint watches it being poured.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone restless and eager who can't wait is impatient, an idiomatic equivalent.

parts.note: as means like, in the same way as
Kew Gardens in west London is the famous botanical garden

explanation.surface: A garden with plants growing at odd angles.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW is the Royal Botanic Gardens in south-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Something askew is at a slant, not straight, which is crooked.

parts.note: a beggar who says he cannot mend his ways offers the excuse that splits as ...

explanation.surface: What a vagrant says when excusing himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as 'mend? I can't': the excuse of someone who will not fix things and must beg.
explanation.definitionFit: A mendicant is someone who lives by begging, especially a member of a begging religious order.

indicators.note: in puts the service inside the transport

parts.note: a bus is a form of public transport
RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A writer of verse working in public transport.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Burns is Scotland's national poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Burns, the eighteenth-century Scottish writer of verse, is an example of a poet.

clue.text: Disfigurement at church is seldom found

indicators.note: the clue says this word placed at the church gives the rare thing, so the church is taken off it

parts.note: something scarce is rarely found
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Blemishes are rarely seen on churches.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as an equation: the answer at CE is SCARCE, so removing CE from SCARCE leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a mark left on the skin by an injury, which disfigures it.

indicators.note: in puts the alien within the rain

parts.note: the wet is rain, rainy weather
ET, the film's extraterrestrial, is crossword shorthand for an alien

explanation.surface: Don't let the extraterrestrial out in the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: To retain something is to continue possessing it, a direct synonym.

indicators.note: holds means the worker contains the job

parts.note: the worker ant is crossword shorthand for a worker
a chore is a tedious or hard task

explanation.surface: A churchworker taking on a hard task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Religious' is a noun here, as in 'a religious', a person in holy orders.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchoret is a hermit living apart for prayer, so a religious recluse.

indicators.note: without means the A is taken out

parts.note: a road is a way

explanation.surface: A route with nowhere to sit.
explanation.walkthrough: A perch, also called a pole, is an old measure of length, five and a half yards.
explanation.definitionFit: The rod, the pole and the perch are the same old unit of measure, so they are synonyms.

parts.note: taken as written
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: Walking all the way to Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Toes are the digits found on a foot, so a toe is something on the foot.

indicators.note: captures means the girl holds the rebel inside

parts.note: Amy is a girl's name
Jack Cade led the 1450 rebellion in Kent

explanation.surface: A pupil seizes a troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Schoolgirl' looks like one word but splits into the definition and the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy is a place of learning, an institution such as a school.

definitions.meaning: the powder left after burning is what remains
the timber of a common deciduous tree of the olive family

explanation.surface: What a wood fire perhaps leaves behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is both the residue of combustion and the hard timber of the tree Fraxinus.

indicators.note: cut here means docked, losing its opening letter

parts.note: a lawn is an area of grass

explanation.surface: Is this what mown grass is?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the whole clue as definition too: the bristle is part of a grass plant.
explanation.definitionFit: An awn is the fine bristle on the head of grasses such as barley, a piece of grass.

clue.text: Starts to make off very easily?

definitions.text: Starts to make off very easily?

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: Is getting away a simple matter once begun?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also hints at the meaning: to make off is to get moving.
explanation.definitionFit: To make off is to leave, to get going, which is to move away.

indicators.note: in revolt means the letters rise up and overturn their order

explanation.surface: A Spanish nobleman, furious, joins an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee is a Spanish or Portuguese nobleman of the highest rank, a prince of Iberia.

clue.text: Some of M25, now and then?

definitions.text: Some of M25, now and then?

parts.words: Some of M25, now and then?
parts.note: parts of the London orbital motorway, when traffic is jammed, become places nobody can drive through

explanation.surface: Stretches of a busy motorway at certain times.
explanation.walkthrough: The M25 is the motorway ringing London, notorious for jams that leave sections at a standstill.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-go area is a place one cannot or should not enter, which a gridlocked motorway is at times.

clue.text: Distress with time and money abroad

parts.note: the rouble is the currency of Russia, foreign money

explanation.surface: Anxiety over time and money on a foreign trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble is worry or difficulty, a synonym of distress.

indicators.note: across means the city spans the letter for Germany

parts.note: Hanover is a city in Lower Saxony
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: Moving from one city to another in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A handover is the passing of control or possession to another, which is a transfer.

clue.text: A way to unknown lack of care

parts.note: a path is a way
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A route to the unknown, taken without concern.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is indifference, the absence of interest or concern.

clue.text: Numerical structure heard in church office

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken as spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a deanery is the office or residence of a dean

explanation.surface: A building's layout as reported in a church office.
explanation.definitionFit: Denary means based on ten, the decimal system of counting, a numerical structure.

clue.text: Some can go crazy over a drink

indicators.note: over means the stretch taken is turned around
some means only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A few people may go wild after drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes CANGOC from the clue and 'over' turns it back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a French brandy, an example of a drink.

indicators.note: without means the A is dropped

parts.note: a cleaver is a butcher's chopper

explanation.surface: Clever enough to manage without an axe.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever and smart both mean quick-witted and intelligent.

indicators.note: imperfect means the musical interval is not properly in order, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A badly sung octave is jeered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the bird' means is booed, which disguises the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a wading bird with an upturned bill.

definitions.meaning: pollution or a trace of corruption
the dialect or vulgar form of is not, as spoken in common speech

explanation.surface: Pollution is rare.
explanation.definitionFit: Taint is a contaminating trace, and tain't is the colloquial contraction for it is not.

clue.text: Tourer man crashed over the line

indicators.note: a crashed car is wrecked, so the letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A driver crashed his touring car across the finishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: In a fraction the top number sits over the dividing line.
explanation.definitionFit: The numerator is the figure written above the bar of a fraction, so it is over the line.

clue.text: Fascinate when about to inflict injury

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
to harm is to inflict injury

explanation.surface: Captivating someone just before hurting them.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm is to delight or captivate, which is to fascinate.

parts.note: a flag hoisted in harbour shows a ship is about to leave

explanation.walkthrough: The blue-and-white signal flag is flown when a vessel is ready to sail; 'off' suggests spoilt food.
explanation.definitionFit: The blue peter is the signal flag P, raised to show a ship is about to put to sea.
